title: Uniform Frobenius bound for normalized inseparable base change of a normal scheme
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral finite-type $k$-scheme, and $l/k$ a finite purely inseparable extension. Set $T=(S\times_k\operatorname{Spec}l)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and let $B$ be its normalization, with composite $q:B\to T\to S\times_k\operatorname{Spec}l\to S$. Then $T$ and $B$ are integral, $q$ is finite, surjective and radicial, and the induced function-field extension $k(B)/k(S)$ is finite purely inseparable.

There is also the following uniform affine assertion. If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and $N\geq0$ satisfies $\lambda^{p^N}\in k$ for every $\lambda\in l$, then for every nonempty affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $S$, put $R=(C\otimes_kl)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and let $D$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $\operatorname{Frac}R$. The inverse image $q^{-1}U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}D$, the canonical map $C\to D$ is injective and finite, and $d^{p^N}\in C$ for every $d\in D$. For each prime ideal $P$ of $C$ the unique prime ideal of $D$ above it is $\{d\in D:d^{p^N}\in P\}$. Its residue-field extension has exponent at most $N$, and every element of $k(B)$ has its $p^N$-th power in $k(S)$. Such an $N$ exists for every finite purely inseparable $l/k$. In characteristic zero $l=k$ and $q$ is an isomorphism.

Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains; radicial means injective on points with purely inseparable residue-field extensions, equivalently universally injective. Schemes, fields, integrality, finite type, base change, reduction, normalization, finite morphisms, surjectivity, radicial morphisms, function fields, normal rings and purely inseparable extensions use [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], [def-sc-normalization], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-radicial-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

proof.text: First assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$. Choose a finite $k$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $l$. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], choose $n_i$ with $e_i^{p^{n_i}}\in k$, and put $N_0=\max_i n_i$. For $\lambda=\sum_i a_i e_i$ one has $\lambda^{p^{N_0}}=\sum_i a_i^{p^{N_0}}e_i^{p^{N_0}}\in k$. Thus a uniform exponent exists. For the rest of the positive-characteristic proof fix ANY exponent $N$ in the statement, and put $Q=p^N$; we do not increase it.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields, last paragraph: existence of a common power for a finite purely inseparable extension

proof.text: Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}C\subset S$ be any nonempty affine open. Integrality makes $C$ a domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], each localization $C_P$ is the corresponding local ring of $S$, hence is a normal domain by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] to the maximal ideals of $C$: $C$ is integrally closed in $K=\operatorname{Frac}C$. This argument also applies in characteristic zero.

source.place: Tag 030B, lemma-normality-is-local, (3) implies (1); schemes.tex Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves

proof.text: By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], $S\times_k\operatorname{Spec}l\to S$ is a homeomorphism. Reduction leaves its underlying space unchanged by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], so $T$ is nonempty and irreducible; being reduced, it is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. A finite affine cover of $S$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras gives a finite affine cover of $T$ by the quotients $(C\otimes_k l)_{\mathrm{red}}$, finitely generated over $l$ by the images of the generators of $C$. Thus $T$ is finite type over $l$. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field); [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives that $T$ is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields, affine proof specialized to a finite purely inseparable extension and a normal source

proof.text: On the chosen chart put $A=C\otimes_k l$ and $R=A/\sqrt{(0)}$, the coordinate ring of the inverse image in $T$. The map $C\to A$, $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, is injective: choose a $k$-linear map $h:l\to k$ with $h(1)=1$, and $1_C\otimes h$ is a left inverse. If the image of $c$ is nilpotent in $A$, then injectivity gives $c^m=0$ in the domain $C$, hence $c=0$. Therefore $C\to R$ is injective. For $a=\sum_i c_i\otimes\lambda_i$ the Frobenius identity gives $a^Q=\sum_i c_i^Q\otimes\lambda_i^Q\in C\otimes1$. Passing to the quotient gives $r^Q\in C$ for EVERY $r\in R$. Also a $k$-basis of $l$ gives finite $C$-module generators $1\otimes e_i$ for $A$, whose images generate $R$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sc-normalization-exists] to the integral finite-type $l$-scheme $T$: $
u:B	o T$ is finite and surjective. Its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] has just one component, $T$ itself with its reduced induced structure (the vanishing ideal of $T$ is the nilradical, which is zero), so it is the normalization of [def-sc-normalization]. The scheme $T$ is reduced and irreducible, so every quasi-compact open of $T$ has exactly one irreducible component. On $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset T$ the nonzerodivisors of the domain $R$ are its nonzero elements, so its total ring of fractions is $L=\operatorname{Frac}R$. Hence [lem-sfb-normalization-affine-total-fractions] identifies $
u^{-1}(W)=q^{-1}(U)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D$ over $W$, where $D$ is the integral closure of $R$ in $L$, with structural map the inclusion $R	o D$. The ring $D$ is a domain, being a subring of the field $L$. Since $
u$ is finite, $R	o D$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Combined with the finite $C$-generators of $R$ from the preceding step this proves that $D$ is finite over $C$: the products of $C$-generators of $R$ and $R$-generators of $D$ generate $D$ over $C$. Thus $q$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0C3N, lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields, affine proof specialized to a finite purely inseparable extension and a normal source

proof.text: The charts $\operatorname{Spec}D$ show that $B$ is reduced. Each is nonempty and irreducible, and two such open charts intersect: their target opens in the integral $T$ intersect and $\nu$ is surjective. Their union is irreducible, since any two nonempty opens of $B$ meet by first intersecting within these irreducible overlapping open charts. Hence $B$ is integral. The inclusions $C\subset R\subset D\subset L$ give the claimed injectivity of $C\to D$, and $R\subset D\subset\operatorname{Frac}R$ gives $\operatorname{Frac}D=L$.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields, affine proof specialized to a finite purely inseparable extension and a normal source

proof.text: For any $x=a/b\in L$ with $a,b\in R$ and $b\ne0$, the preceding power calculation gives $x^Q=a^Q/b^Q\in K$; the denominator is nonzero since $R$ is a domain. Now take $d\in D$ and a monic equation $d^m+\sum_{i<m}r_i d^i=0$ with $r_i\in R$. Raising it to the $Q$-th power gives $(d^Q)^m+\sum_{i<m}r_i^Q(d^Q)^i=0$, whose coefficients lie in $C$. We have just proved $d^Q\in K$, so normality of $C$ puts $d^Q$ in $C$ by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. This proves the bound with the originally specified $N$, on every nonempty affine open.

source.place: Tag 0C3N, lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields, affine proof specialized to a finite purely inseparable extension and a normal source

proof.text: For a prime $P\subset C$ define $J_P=\{d\in D:d^Q\in P\}$. The map $F:D\to C$, $d\mapsto d^Q$, is a unital ring homomorphism, so $J_P=F^{-1}(P)$ is prime. For $c\in C$, $c^Q\in P$ if and only if $c\in P$, so $J_P\cap C=P$. Conversely, if $J\subset D$ is any prime contracting to $P$, then $d\in J$ if and only if $d^Q\in J\cap C=P$, since $Q>0$. Hence $J=J_P$, proving the displayed formula and bijectivity on points. Every element of $\kappa(J_P)=\operatorname{Frac}(D/J_P)$ is $\bar a/\bar b$ with $b\notin J_P$; its $Q$-th power is the image of $\overline{a^Q}/\overline{b^Q}\in\operatorname{Frac}(C/P)=\kappa(P)$, with nonzero denominator by the formula for $J_P$. Thus the residue extension has exponent at most $N$. The chartwise conclusions give global surjectivity and radiciality of $q$, using [def-weil-radicial-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0BRA, lemma-p-ring-map, proof, with the fixed-power prime and residue-field calculation written explicitly

proof.text: By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] applied to the nonempty affine charts of $S$ and $B$, the induced function fields are $k(S)=\operatorname{Frac}C=K$ and $k(B)=\operatorname{Frac}D=L$, with their structural inclusion. Apply [lem-trf-finite-domain-fraction-degree] to the injective finite map $C\to D$: $L/K$ is finite. Step 7 gives $x^{p^N}\in K$ for every $x\in L$, which makes $L/K$ purely inseparable by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

source.place: Tag 0C3N, lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields, affine proof specialized to a finite purely inseparable extension and a normal source

proof.text: Finally suppose $\operatorname{char}k=0$. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] one has $l=k$, and $T=S$ since $S$ is reduced. The affine normality argument of step 2 gives that each $C$ equals its integral closure in $\operatorname{Frac}C$. Since $S$ is integral, each quasi-compact open of $S$ has one irreducible component and the total ring of fractions of $C$ is $\operatorname{Frac}C$; as in step 5 the componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization] of $S$ is its normalization, and on these charts [lem-sfb-normalization-affine-total-fractions] therefore makes $B\to S$ the identity $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}C$. These canonical identifications agree as the inverse of $q$, so $q$ is an isomorphism. The assertions of integrality, finiteness, surjectivity, radiciality and the trivial finite purely inseparable function-field extension follow immediately.
